title: Parents
hook: honor them, including when it's complicated
tomorrow: why do brothers in the Bible fight so much?

segments.voice: Yesterday, children: Jesus stood a child in the middle and let the child be the lesson. A child teaches. Today, the people who were the grown-ups in your story.

A text from a parent: call me when you can. Your stomach does something before you even know why. Maybe it's love, maybe it's an old argument, maybe both. So what do you owe a parent when it's complicated? The commandment is short, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Honour thy father and thy mother." Notice what it doesn't say. It doesn't say agree with them. It doesn't say like them every day. It says honor.
screen: `CALL ME WHEN YOU CAN.` → `HONOR YOUR FATHER AND MOTHER.` → `NOT AGREE. NOT LIKE. HONOR.`

segments.voice: Luke tells a story where honor and honesty sit in the same scene. Jesus is twelve. His parents lose him on the road home from Jerusalem and find him days later in the Temple. His mother says what any parent would: we've been looking for you, sick with worry. He answers honestly: didn't you know I had to be in my Father's house? They don't understand him. And then, in the Douay-Rheims words: "he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them." Both things, in one family. Luke adds that his mother kept all these words in her heart. She didn't understand her son yet, and she didn't stop holding on to him either. Honesty on one side, patience on the other, and nobody walks out. The Catechism draws the same lines. Children living at home obey their parents in what is good, but if conscience says an order is wrong, they must not follow it. Grown children owe respect, gratitude, and help when parents are old, sick or lonely. The book of Sirach adds patience: if a father's understanding fails, don't look down on him. So honor isn't pretending, and it isn't a performance of agreement at the dinner table. It's telling the truth and staying respectful while you do. And if a parent caused real harm, honor can be as small as a prayer said from a safe distance.
screen: `I MUST BE IN MY FATHER'S HOUSE.` · `HE WENT DOWN WITH THEM.` · `OBEY, UNLESS CONSCIENCE SAYS NO.` · `RESPECT, GRATITUDE, HELP.` · then, large: `HONOR, HONESTLY.`

segments.voice: Say your parents' names out loud, quietly, one at a time, living or gone, and the names of anyone who raised you. After each name, let one true thing come up, a thank-you or a hurt, without arguing with it. If you pray, pray for each of them by name, just as they are today.
Parents. The ones the commandment asks you to honor, not to pretend about. Today's word.
Your line: honor, honestly. At twelve, Jesus told the truth and still went home with them. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics count honoring father and mother among the Ten Commandments; the Catechism spells it out as respect, gratitude, obedience at home within the limits of conscience, and care for parents in old age.

myth: the commandment says obey your father and mother
it says honor. the Catechism adds that conscience comes first when an order is wrong.
in Luke, the twelve-year-old Jesus went home and was subject to his parents
after telling them honestly where he had to be.
the Catechism says grown children owe nothing more once they leave home
it names respect, gratitude, and help in old age, sickness and loneliness.

options: repost one now and then so she feels supported.
mute her, and quietly stop bringing it up at all.
tell her privately and kindly, and keep calling her.
fork.reveal: honor isn't pretending, and it isn't pulling away. in Luke, Jesus says the honest thing and still goes home with his parents.

chat.says: told dad about the club tryout in austin. he said "we'll see" and went quiet. so honor means drop it?
options: No. Tell him honestly why it matters, then really listen. Jesus did both at twelve.
Yes. Honor means obeying, so let it go unless he brings it up again.
No. You're nearly grown, so honoring him is more of a choice now.
chat.meaning: Honor isn't silence or pretending. In Luke, Jesus says the honest thing to his parents and still goes home with them.

Temple.meaning: the great house of worship in Jerusalem

Nazareth.meaning: the small town in Galilee where Jesus grew up

Catechism.meaning: the Church's official summary of what Catholics believe

Sirach.meaning: a book of wisdom sayings in the Catholic Bible
